title: Composition of proper morphisms of algebraic spaces
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Give spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For morphisms of spaces, separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Locally of finite type and locally of finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed, where universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (agreeing with the scheme convention [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Let $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z$ be composable morphisms of algebraic spaces. If $u$ and $v$ are proper, then $v\circ u$ is proper. No local Noetherian, local quasi-finiteness, representability, or finite-presentation assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Properness gives separatedness of $u$ and $v$. Apply the separated-composition clause of [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] to $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z$, over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. It gives that $v\circ u$ is separated. Only that clause is used: neither finite presentation nor representability is assumed.

Properness also gives local finite type and quasi-compactness for $u,v$. The local-finite-type composition clause of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], including its explicit agreement with the ordinary algebraic-space chart notion, gives local finite type for $v\circ u$. For quasi-compactness in the convention stated in this item, let $W\subseteq |Z|$ be a quasi-compact open. Then $|v|^{-1}(W)$ is a quasi-compact open, and $|u|^{-1}(|v|^{-1}(W))$ is quasi-compact, by the two hypotheses; it equals $|v\circ u|^{-1}(W)$. Thus the composite is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 04XY, using Tag 03XG (lemma-composition-finite-type); the chart-composition input is also stated in stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06FT (lemma-composition-finite-type).

proof.text: Fix any algebraic-space base change $T\to Z$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $Y_T=Y\times_ZT$ and $X_T=X\times_ZT$ are algebraic spaces. The universal property identifies $X\times_YY_T$ with $X_T$: both represent pairs of maps into $X$ and $T$ whose composites to $Z$ agree. Hence $X_T\to Y_T$ is a base change of $u$, and $Y_T\to T$ is a base change of $v$. Both induce closed maps on point spaces by universal closedness of $u,v$. If $C\subseteq |X_T|$ is closed, its image in $|Y_T|$ is closed, and the image of that closed set in $|T|$ is closed. This last image is the image of $C$ under $|(v\circ u)_T|$, since maps on field-valued point classes compose. Thus every base change of $v\circ u$ is closed, which is precisely universal closedness. This writes out the omitted proof of Tag 03IU.

source.place: Tag 04XY, using Tag 03IU (lemma-composition-universally-closed), whose omitted proof is expanded directly from the definition.

proof.text: The composite is separated by step 1, of finite type by step 2, and universally closed by step 3. These are the three defining conditions for properness stated in the item, so $v\circ u$ is proper.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04XY (lemma-composition-proper), its three cited stability lemmas; Tag 03IU expanded from definitions.
